chapter: New Orleans, Havana and back to New York
title: Back to California in 1932: sideline movie work and the Long Beach earthquake
summary: He did on-screen band-directing in films such as Love and Hisses and Sally, Irene and Mary, and left before the earthquake; Willard shows him a book listing his film appearances.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: So when you got back from Cuba, where did you go?

I got my situation straightened away and I went back to New York and let's see, oh, somewhere in there I had been to California again. You say Cuba, see, we got all the way up to Cuba, which is '35, I was back in California in '32.

And that was the time when I did a little extra work. Well, not extra work, but what they call sideline. I mean when they'd have an orchestra in a picture, the music was recorded by the studio orchestra, and then they would have -- I would be the guy standing there directing the band, you know. I did a little bit of that, and I got out of there just ahead of the earthquake.
Oh, "Love and Hisses," and "Sally, Irene and Mary," and --
There's a new book out called, "Jazz in the Movies," and see those markers? Every one of those is a movie Charlie Barnet is in.
I didn't realize I was in that many.
They must be counting shorts, then, too.
